change.author: Udit Takkar

findings.title: Reminders of users locked for SMS are deleted silently after two cron runs
findings.body: `twilio.scheduleSMS` returns `undefined` when `isLockedForSMSSending` is true (twilioProvider.ts:92-95). Before this change, those reminders stayed unscheduled and were picked up again once the user or team was unlocked. Now each cron run bumps `retryCount`, and the `retryCount > 1` branch of the `deleteMany` (line 39-41) removes the row on the second run after that. The reminder is permanently lost, with no log and no state visible to the user. The lock is an admin or billing state that can last much longer than two cron intervals. Either don't count the locked case as a retry (skip the update and just `continue`), or log the drop so it is visible.

findings.title: retryCount delete clause has no method filter and drops rows after only two failures
findings.body: The second `OR` branch is `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` with no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` filter, so it matches any WorkflowReminder (email, WhatsApp) whose `retryCount` exceeds 1. Today only this handler writes `retryCount`, so nothing else matches, but the column is generic and a later writer would have its rows deleted by the SMS cron. Add `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` to that branch. Also, `gt: 1` gives a reminder only two attempts, so a short Twilio outage or a rate-limit error (`checkSMSRateLimit` throws at twilioProvider.ts:98) can permanently drop reminders that are still days from being due. Consider a higher threshold, named as a constant.

findings.title: DB update inside catch can throw and abort the whole batch
findings.body: The `prisma.workflowReminder.update` in the `catch` block is not guarded. If the DB call fails (the likely cause when the original error was a DB error too), the exception escapes the `for` loop. The remaining reminders are not processed and the handler returns a 500. Wrap the update in its own try/catch, or log and continue. Also, `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` uses the value read at the start of the run, so overlapping cron runs can lose increments. `{ increment: 1 }` avoids that. The same update appears twice (lines 179 and 190), and a small helper would remove the duplication.

contracts.action: New retryCount increment when twilio.scheduleSMS returns undefined, and in the catch block
contracts.equivalent_path: Previously a falsy scheduleSMS result did nothing and the row stayed scheduled=false for the next cron run. The existing success path (line 169-177) updates scheduled and referenceId.
contracts.before_after: Before: the reminder was retried on every cron run until its scheduledDate passed. After: each failure increments retryCount, and the next run's deleteMany removes rows with retryCount>1.
contracts.visible_effect: Reminders for locked users or users hitting errors are deleted after two failed runs, so the attendee never gets the SMS.
contracts.failure_mode: The update in the catch block is unguarded, so a DB failure aborts the loop and later reminders are not processed in that run. scheduleSMS returns undefined only for the SMS-locked case (twilioProvider.ts:92-95), and every other failure throws.

contracts.before_after: The whole retry is bounded by retryCount > 1, so at most 2 failed attempts per reminder across cron runs. Inside a run the loop is sequential over all unscheduled reminders, and the Twilio calls have no per-call timeout.
contracts.visible_effect: A slow Twilio response delays the whole cron request. The cron handler has no deadline.
contracts.failure_mode: Not a new problem, since the loop was already sequential. The retry counter does not bound time within a run.

summary: The retry-count migration and schema column look fine. The handler has two real problems. A reminder for a user or team locked for SMS now gets deleted after two cron runs, silently, where before it stayed queued until the lock cleared. The new `retryCount > 1` delete clause also has no `method` filter and gives each reminder only two attempts. A smaller issue: the unguarded DB update in the `catch` can abort the rest of the batch.
